newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Gasoline demand features in API report.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Gasoline demand features in API report.

text.p: REUTER SURVEY ESTIMATES* ACTUAL STOCKS FOR
FOR WEEK ENDED 07/11/97 WEEK ENDED 07/11/97-CHANGE
DISTILLATE...... UP 2.00 MLN 121,389 UP 5.457 MLN
GASOLINE........ DN 2.00 MLN 200,597 DN 3.498 MLN
UTILIZATION..... UNCH PCT PT 96.8 UP 1.2 PCT PT
*NB - The survey estimate is derived by omitting the high and low forecast and averaging the rest, with a sample of at least six.
Gasoline demand, running at a very high rate, was the feature of the latest American Petroleum Institute weekly report, analysts and traders said Tuesday.

Most said they will wait for confirmation from Wednesday's Department of Energy report on the rate of gasoline demand. But even if it is confirmed, analysts said they don't see the rate as sustainable.

The "implied demand," a calculation based on 3.5 million-barrel drawdown in inventory, 184,000 barrels per day (bpd) imports and just over eight million bpd production, was some 8.685 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ended July 11, the API reported.

"Demand is extraordinarily high. On a four-week average year-on-year it is up 3.6 percent," said Nizam Sharief, director of energy research at consultant Hornsby & Co in Houston. That is up from a 2.8 percent year-on-year growth rate in the second quarter and a decline in the first quarter.

"Continuing strong gasoline demand is one of the main stories of this report," said Thomas Blakeslee, analyst with Cargill Investor Services in New York. "But the distillate build is going to weigh on prices," Blakeslee said.

While gasoline stocks declined to 200.5 million barrels, inventories of distillates -- mainly heating oil and diesel -- rose by more than 5.4 million barrels last week to just over 121 million barrels, or nearly 17 million barrels above year-ago levels, the API showed.

"We've all been waiting for distillates to fall out of bed and they have," said Jim Fiedler of E.D.& F. Man International Inc . Implied demand for heating oil, Fiedler said, came in at about 2.9 million barrels per day, a big drop from 3.7 million last week.

Meanwhile, crude oil stocks declined by 5.4 million barrels, but only by 2.34 million barrels when taking out volatile West Coast stocks. A fall off from the very high import levels into the East of Rockies areas to 7.4 million bpd was a large factor.
But even looking at the bullish gasoline demand, analysts said they didn't expect a very great affect on the market.
"We could see a 50 point gain tomorrow but keep in mind we were sharply up ahead of the APIs and that should limit the upside," said Richard Redash, senior energy analyst at Prudential.

The lower import level this week should rebound and with production still at healthy levels "the outlook is not that bullish for gasoline. Supply seems more than enough to meet demand for the rest of the summer," Redash added.
August gasoline futures were up 0.56 at 60.50 in ACCESS trading on NYMEX early Tuesday evening, having closed in the regular session at 59.94 cents a gallon for a gain 1.59 cents.
Heating oil was down 0.10 at 52.85, having ended 1.28 up at 52.95.
Crude was up six cents at 19.73 having settled up 68 cents at $19.67.
--New York Energy Desk, +1 212 859 1623
